front.title: Environmental Impact Information for In-situ Operations, Administration, and Maintenance (IOAM)

abstract.t: In Situ Operations, Administration, and Maintenance (IOAM) is used for recording and collecting operational and telemetry information while the packet traverses a path between two points in the network. This document defines a type of IOAM Node Data that makes use of the Node Data Fields to help an opoerator gain visibility on environmental sustainability information on the Internet by providing per-hop (i.e., per topological network node) power metrics and other current or future sustainability metrics. This will contribute to achieving an objective mentioned in the IAB E-Impact workshop.

The techniques presented are useful not only in a transactional setting, but also in a scheduled automated setting where they may be run periodically in a mesh across an administrative domain to map out environmental sustainability metrics.

section.name: Motivation
section.t: The IAB held a workshop on "Environmental Impact of Internet Applications and Systems (eimpactws)" [IAB-EIMPACTWS], in which the need for visibility into environmental sustainability metrics within traditional Internet tools was highlighted (see WebVTT cue identifiers 139 and 140 of [IAB-EIMPACTWS-Minutes].)
The Environmental Information Data Fields defined in this document allow appending environmental metrics inside the IOAM packet from each reported node.

And as, In Situ Operations, Administration, and Maintenance (IOAM) is used for recording and collecting operational and telemetry information while the packet traverses a path between two points in the network, using IOAM for delivering environmental sustainability metrics is very effective.

section.title: Introduction
section.t: In situ Operations, Administration, and Maintenance (IOAM) collects operational and telemetry information in the packet while the packet traverses a path between two points in the network. The term "in situ" refers to the fact that the OAM data is added to the data packets rather than being sent within packets specifically dedicated to OAM. IOAM is used to complement mechanisms, such as Ping or Traceroute.

As the world transitions towards sustainability in technology, the focus is shifting not only on creating modern technologies infused with sustainability but also on bridging gaps in the tools that are already available, to enhance visibility, measurement, and quantification of their impact. Consequently, tools which have been foundational for control and management for decades now encounter new requirements including enhancing them to cater to a significantly increasing demand for monitoring the sustainability and environmental impact. This document serves that need by defining an IOAM Node Data that uses the Node Data Fields to gain visibility on environmental sustainability information
By using the combination of IOAM Data Fields, a device can explicitly add these exemplary environmental sustainability metrics for transmission across an administrative domain:

ul.li: Present and idle power (node level, component level)

section.name: Environmental Information Data Field (EID-F)
section.t: The Environmental Information Data Field Structure contains exactly one Environmental Information Header followed by one or more Data Field objects. The Data Field objects comprises a EI Object Header and a EI Object Payload. (EI: Environmental Information)

dl.dd: 4 Bits for representing the version of the Environmental Information Data Field

A 24-bit Length to represent the length of entire Data Field Structure which follows this header. The length field MUST be present and populated with the "number of 4 octect words" in the eintire EID-F Object (this will allow us to have a lot of data in this env object and won't have any problems as we already will have a dedicated object-header which will state the data length anyways) This field will also let the processing node till what size does the EID-F object go to so that it won't accidentally consider the Opaque State Snapshot Data Field as a part of the EID-F.
---------DECIDE ON This-----------
[-- (Two options, 1 to represent the length of the data as is, in terms of bits, 2. to represent length in terms of number of 4 octect words (this will allow us to have a lot of data in this env object and won't have any problems as we already will have a object-header which will state the data length anyways)) --]

dd.t: A 16-Bit Length field to represent the length of the object, measured in octets, including the object header and object payload.
8 Bits EI-Type field to represent the type of Environmental Information that is present in the following EI-object payload

dl.dd: The object payload will be based on the definitions of the EI-Type. Discussed in .

section.name: EI-Type Definitions
section.t: The Environmental Information Type (EI-Type) will define the structure to carry the Environmental Information Object Payload as discussed in .
The following EI-Type values are currently defined.

dd.t: The Present Power is the node-level power being presently drawn, which is a magnitude that may be directly displayed, and is expressed in Watts (W). A value of 0 indicates that the Present Power is not available. The Idle Power is the node-level power when the node is idle. A value of 0 indicates that the Idle Power is not available.
The Length is 12 if the object contains this payload. A Length value of 4 indicates that it is unavailable.

The returned value is the node-level present throughput, which is a magnitude that may be directly displayed, and is expressed in bits-per-second (BPS). This allows the recipient of the ICMP message to determine a relationship between power and traffic load.
This is a 64-bit structure to accomodate high speed interface throughputs as well.

dl.dd: The Length is 12 if the object contains this payload. A Length value of 4 indicates that it is unavailable.

dl.dt: Ecolabels and Environmentally Relevant Certification (EERC) EI-Object

figure.name: Ecolabels and Environmentally Relevant Certification (EERC) EI-Object

dd.t: The returned value references an Ecolabels and Environmentally Relevant Certification (EERC) number.
The following EERC numbers are defined by the present specification:
The "Year" field must contain the year in which the certificate was issued, or 0 to indicate "unknown" or "not specified".

dl.dd: The Length is 8 if the object contains this payload. A Length value of 4 indicates that it is unavailable.

dd.t: The returned value is one or more instances of component-level power drawn metrics. Each instance is a set comprised by a UUID uniquely identifying the component, and the Present Component Power and Idle Component Power fields.
The Present Component Power is the component-level power being presently drawn, which is a magnitude that may be directly displayed, and is expressed in Watts (W).

A value of 0 indicates that the Present Component Power is not available. The Idle Component Power is the component-level power when the component is idle. A value of 0 indicates that the Idle Component Power is not available.

dl.dd: The Length is 4 plus 20 times the number of elements included. A Length value of 4 indicates that this object is unavailable.

dd.t: The returned value is one or more instances of component-level throughput. Each instance is a set comprised by a UUID uniquely identifying the component, and the actual throughput of said component in bits-per-second (BPS). This allows the recipient of the ICMP message to determine a relationship between power and traffic load.
The Length is 12 if the object contains this payload. A Length value of 4 indicates that it is unavailable.

dl.dd: The Length is 4 plus 24 times the number of elements included. A Length value of 4 indicates that this object is unavailable.
